Mousy

MOW-see · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Mousy is nervous, shy, or meek, often in a quiet or unremarkable way.

The mousy clerk avoided eye contact with every customer who raised their voice.

Worked Example

Colleagues were shocked when the mousy accountant stood up and confidently challenged the CEO's numbers.

The surprise came precisely because the accountant was normally so meek and unassuming -- exactly what mousy describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shy: showing a lack of courage or confidence

meek: quiet and gentle, easily overshadowed

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

bold: confident and unafraid of attention

Where it sits · how strong the timidity is — shy → mousy → fearful

shy vs. mousy: Shy just means uncomfortable in social situations; mousy adds a sense of being easy to overlook entirely.

fearful vs. mousy: Mousy describes a quiet, unassuming personality; fearful describes active fear or dread in a specific moment.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — mous

root — mous: a small, meek rodent (Old English (mus))

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: having the quality of (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Mousy simply combines mouse with -y, 'having the quality of' -- comparing a shy, easily-overlooked person to the small, meek animal.

Use the root in a new word: mouse

Use the root in a new word: mouse: Mouse itself is one of English's oldest surviving animal words, essentially unchanged from Old English mus.

Word Choice

Mousy can describe a person's personality (shy, meek) or, less often, a dull grayish-brown hair color -- both senses come from the same comparison to a mouse.
